commit_subject: (screen-flagged) b1.6 certify (PR #1300): diff changes the Brazil gate in every generated composition from `not entry_is_line_b` to `not entry_is_section_232_aluminum` and re-grounds the steel parameter proof from 9903.81.87/.88 to 9903.82.02; report says "The task's 9903.81.x locator is stale for this corpus vintage".
description: The generated compositions move from the witness's five per-line exemplar flags to membership-semantic caller inputs, and gain a Section 232 steel component the witness never had.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The Brazil IEEPA surcharge carve-out was conditioned on `entry_is_line_b` - the witness's identity flag for HTS 7601.10.30.00 - a per-line exemplar predicate with no basis in HTS 9903.01.77's exclusion, instead of on the Section 232 aluminum membership the source's excluded heading 9903.01.83 actually turns on.
triage.triage_notes: Same pattern as index 24 (changed lines byte-identical modulo chapter token and paren depth). Chapter 27 is mineral fuels, so the energy-resource branches sit elsewhere in the module and were untouched by this commit. Corpus reads and source reasoning are recorded at index 24.
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as a mere input-surface generalization and could not: the diff changes the operative gate of `ieepa_component_rate` and `ieepa_component_rate_with_declared_exceptions` from `not entry_is_line_b` — the witness harness's identity flag for the single exemplar line 7601.10.30.00, a caller input with no definition or meaning inside a generated chapter-27 module — to `not entry_is_section_232_aluminum`, a membership predicate. Read through the pinned release, HTS 9903.01.77 states "Except for products described in headings 9903.01.78-9903.01.83 and 9903.01.90, articles the product of Brazil…", and 9903.01.83 carves out "Articles of iron or steel; derivative articles of iron or steel; articles of aluminum; derivative articles of aluminum…", i.e. a class membership, never a per-line identity; the module's own proof atom for this rule is a `kind: exception` atom quoting that the 9903.01.77 duties "shall not apply to products of aluminum provided for in heading 9903.85.02". So the pre-fix condition had no basis in the cited source and the fix re-grounds it on the class the source actually uses — untraceable_branch, not amount, boundary, polarity, or a missing clause. The other half of the diff (steel citation 9903.81.87/.88 → 9903.82.02) is provenance-only and does not carry the verdict.

triage.verifier_notes: (1) The first reader's quote is the PR body's lede and describes PR #1300 as a whole, most of which landed in the PARENT commit a9562cfd ("b1.6: generalize generated component surfaces") — that commit already swapped entry_is_line_b → entry_is_section_232_aluminum in section_232_aluminum_component_rate and added the steel component with the 9903.81.87/.88 citations. This commit is the leftover: the generator's substitution map (tools/generate_schedule_compositions.py lines 99-100) already contained the ieepa_component_rate entries at the parent, but the parent's emitted YAML was stale for those two rules; the certify re-emit applied them. A commit-scoped quote is the diff line, not the PR lede. (2) The steel hunks (source string + proof-atom corpus_citation_path/excerpt 9903.81.87/.88 → 9903.82.02, two atoms collapsed to one) are mechanical provenance: `formula: '0.50'` is byte-identical, and B16-C-REPORT.md says "The task's 9903.81.x locator is stale for this corpus vintage: Rev. 15 contains no operative 9903.81.x row and consolidates the charge at 9903.82.02." If this case is later split per-hunk, that half is mechanical. (3) Residual issues a reviewer may want: the post-fix predicate is still under-inclusive versus 9903.01.83, which also excludes iron/steel and derivatives, wood products, vehicles and parts, semiconductor articles and copper — only aluminum is gated; and `entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded` still carries `formula: entry_is_line_b` in the post file (line 1924), a surviving exemplar coupling under a rule sourced to "HTS 9903.01.33 section 232 metals article scope". (4) Runtime impact within ch27 itself is probably nil (mineral fuels; no §232 aluminum lines, and entry_is_line_b would default false), so the correction is to encoded meaning rather than to any ch27 number — this is the main reason I held confidence at 0.75 rather than higher; the same generated formula in ch76 is where the carve-out would actually misfire. (5) The module's proof-atom excerpt is cited to us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-219, which in the pinned release (us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap, HTS 2026 Rev 3 notes) resolves to a list of derivative HTS numbers, not that sentence — page numbering differs from the Rev. 15 vintage the module claims. The substance is independently confirmed by 9903.01.77 and 9903.01.83 themselves, but the page-level locator does not verify.
